beats.narration_text: Retrieval is built on an assumption nobody says out loud: that a document is text. Most of the documents worth retrieving aren't. They're tables, charts and code — and the standard pipeline destroys precisely those. I'm Anjana.

show.event: ClaudeComposerAsk: greeting 'Hello, Anjana'; ask types itself
runningText 'reading the whole page…'
output lines resolve, already answered

props.command: Standard RAG embeds text and retrieves text. But the documents I actually care about are full of tables, charts and code blocks. What happens to those in a normal pipeline, and what would it take to retrieve them as what they are rather than as flattened text?
output: the chunker classifies before it splits
each non-text type gets its own translation step

beats.narration_text: Most RAG systems treat every document as a wall of text. They strip out formatting, flatten tables into rows of words, ignore charts entirely, and turn code blocks into paragraphs. The information is still there — technically — but the structure that gave it meaning is gone. A revenue table becomes a jumble of numbers without column headers. A flowchart becomes nothing. A code function loses its indentation and syntax. Text-only chunking destroys exactly the content that's hardest to reconstruct.

show.event: the source document appears with four colour-coded regions
an arrow draws into the text-only chunker
the paragraph comes out intact, ticked
the table comes out as one flat string of numbers, no headers
the chart comes out as an empty gap — image removed
the code comes out unindented, one paragraph
the three failure marks pulse together

beats.narration_text: Layout-aware chunking solves the first problem: it sees the page as a human does. Instead of splitting on token count alone, it detects content boundaries — where a paragraph ends and a table begins, where a code block starts, where a figure sits. Each content type becomes its own chunk with a type label attached. A table chunk preserves rows, columns, and headers. A code chunk keeps indentation and language tags. The chunker doesn't just split text — it classifies what it's splitting.

show.event: the same page appears
a fixed-token grid overlays it, cutting through the table and the code
the grid is struck out
dashed boxes draw around each content region, following its edges
type labels stamp on: text, table, image, code
arrows run to four chunk cards on the right
each card appears with its content intact and its type tag
the type tags pulse

beats.narration_text: Non-text content needs a translation step before it can be embedded. Tables go through structured extraction — the raw grid becomes a schema-aware representation with column types, row relationships, and summary statistics. Charts and diagrams are processed by a vision-language model that generates a text description capturing the visual's key information: axes, trends, labels, relationships. Code blocks are parsed into an abstract syntax tree, then summarized as a natural language description of what the function does, its inputs, and its outputs. Each extraction creates a retrievable text representation without losing the original.

show.event: three lanes appear: table, chart, code
the table flows into structured extraction
a schema-aware JSON emerges with column types and a summary
the chart flows into the vision-language model
a text description emerges naming axes and trends
the code flows into the AST parser
a summary emerges with inputs, outputs and behaviour
'original preserved' resolves on all three lanes

beats.narration_text: Now each chunk has a text representation that can be embedded — but not all embeddings are equal. Text chunks use a standard text embedding model. Table summaries may use the same model or a specialized one trained on structured data. Image descriptions embed alongside their source metadata. Code summaries can use a code-aware embedding model that understands programming semantics. At retrieval time, the query matches against all modalities. A question about revenue trends might retrieve a text paragraph, a revenue table, and a bar chart — all from different pages, all relevant, all preserving their original format for the language model.

show.event: four embedding lanes appear, each with its chunk type
the code lane routes to a different, code-aware embedder
all four vectors converge into the unified index
the index fills with mixed-colour vectors
a query enters: what drove revenue growth in Q3?
three cards fan out — a paragraph, the table, the chart
relevance scores resolve on each card
the cards feed the model, which answers from all three
ClaudeTitleOutro: title in serif, terracotta period
subline fades in
